mainTopic: Aggadot on the מגילה: המן's shame, אסתר before the king, why she invited המן, and the king's sleepless night
overview: This amud keeps explaining the פסוקים of מגילת אסתר, with several side discussions. It starts with המן's shame before מרדכי, who knew him as a former slave sold for bread. It then explains why המן said all his treasures were worth nothing to him. A side teaching on ישעיה 28 says that הקדוש ברוך הוא will be a crown for humble צדיקים. It then shows מדת הדין challenging why ישראל are treated differently from the nations. Back in the מגילה, the שכינה leaves אסתר at the room of idols, and three מלאכים help her before the king, including stretching his scepter. The king offers up to half the kingdom, but not the rebuilding of the בית המקדש. A long list of תנאים and אמוראים give reasons why אסתר invited המן, and אליהו says all of them are true. The amud ends with המן's many sons, the king's sleepless night, and the records that read themselves; the explanation of the word ״כָתוּב״ continues on the next amud.

steps.title: המן was called the slave sold for bread
steps.stepSummary: The previous line ends by saying מרדכי treated המן as someone of poor, lowly background. רב פפא adds that המן was even nicknamed 'the slave sold for a loaf of bread'.
steps.simpleTranslation: …as a poor man. רב פפא said: And they called him 'the slave who was sold for a loaf of bread'.
steps.whatsHappening: The first word closes the previous sentence: מרדכי treated המן like a poor man. Then רב פפא adds a detail about the nickname המן was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that מרדכי knew המן's embarrassing past as a former slave. רב פפא makes this stronger: המן was known as a slave who sold himself for something as cheap as bread. This helps explain why the sight of מרדכי hurt המן so much.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person, someone of lowly background

steps.confusionAlert: The first word, בפרוזבוטי, is the end of a sentence from the previous section. It is not the start of a new idea. רב פפא's statement is the new part.

phrases.english: as a poor man (of lowly background).
phrases.notes: This word finishes the line before it: it's how מרדכי treated המן.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And they called him
the slave who was sold for a loaf of bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the previous statement that מרדכי reminded המן of his lowly past.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן was known as the slave who sold himself for a loaf of bread.

steps.title: המן's treasures engraved on his heart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains המן's words 'all this is worth nothing to me'. המן had a list of all his treasures engraved on his heart. Whenever he saw מרדכי at the king's gate, he said none of it was worth anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And all this is worth nothing to me': this teaches that all the treasures of that wicked man were engraved on his heart. When he saw מרדכי sitting at the king's gate, he said: all this is worth nothing to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a פסוק in מגילת אסתר where המן says all his wealth means nothing to him. It explains what 'all this' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All this' points to something המן carried with him: a record of his treasures engraved over his heart. Seeing מרדכי, who refused to bow and knew his shameful past, made all that wealth feel worthless.

phrases.english: 'And all this is worth nothing to me'
teaches that all the treasures
of that wicked man
were engraved on his heart,
and when he would see Mordecai
sitting at the king's gate,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כׇּל זֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁוֶה לִי.
phrases.english: he said: all this is worth nothing to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל זֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁוֶה לִי מְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining המן's feelings toward מרדכי by reading his words in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'All this' refers to המן's treasures engraved on his heart, which felt worthless whenever he saw מרדכי.

steps.title: God will be a crown for every righteous person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, teaches that in the future הקדוש ברוך הוא will be a crown on the head of every צדיק. He brings a פסוק from ישעיה as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will be a crown on the head of every single צדיק, as it says: 'On that day, ה׳ צבאות will be a crown of glory…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about a crown in the future, probably linked to the earlier topic of crowns and royal glory in the מגילה. It quotes a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן's treasures were worth nothing to him. In contrast, the צדיקים will receive the greatest possible crown: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself. The פסוק's words 'crown of glory' are the base text that the next steps explain word by word.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introducing a פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will be a crown
on the head of each and every righteous person,
as it is said: 'On that day
the Lord of hosts will be
a crown of glory, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching from the same chain of אמוראים, moving from המן to the reward of the צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will be a crown on the head of every צדיק.

steps.title: What do 'crown of glory' and 'diadem of beauty' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the double phrase in the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up an explanation of the פסוק's unusual words. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two descriptions that seem to say the same thing. The גמרא wants to know what each word adds. The words צבי and צפירת are about to be read as hints to two kinds of people.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'a crown of glory'
and a diadem of beauty'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לַעֲטֶרֶת צְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the words צבי and צפירת תפארה in the פסוק.

steps.title: For those who do His will and await His glory
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads צבי as hinting to people who do God's will (צביונו). It reads צפירת as hinting to people who look forward to His glory (מצפין).
steps.simpleTranslation: For those who do His will, and for those who await His glory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question through wordplay. Each word in the פסוק describes a different group that will get the crown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צבי sounds like צביון, meaning will or desire. So the crown is for those who do what God wants. צפירת sounds like מצפה, meaning to look forward to. So the diadem is for those who long for God's glory to be revealed.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who await, look forward to

phrases.english: for those who do His will
and for those who await His glory.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָעוֹשִׂין צִבְיוֹנוֹ וְלַמְצַפִּין תִּפְאַרְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צבי means those who do His will (צביונו). צפירת means those who await His glory (מצפין).

steps.title: Maybe the crown is for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possibility: maybe every person who does God's will and awaits His glory gets this crown.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think it is for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next move. It suggests that the reward might apply to all such people, and the next step will limit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the standard 'יכול' pattern. The גמרא suggests a broad reading so that the פסוק can narrow it. The question is whether doing God's will is enough, or whether something more is required.

phrases.english: One might think it applies to everyone —

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the reward described in step 5 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the reward: who exactly receives the crown.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the crown is for those who do His will, perhaps every such person receives it, with no further condition.

steps.title: Only for those who see themselves as leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'לשאר עמו', meaning 'to the remainder of His people'. This teaches that the crown goes only to someone who sees himself as small, like leftovers.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says 'to the remainder of His people': to someone who regards himself as leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'maybe everyone' suggestion by pointing to the end of the פסוק. The reward is limited to humble people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שאר (remainder) is read as describing the person's attitude. He sees himself like שיריים, the unimportant leftovers. Doing God's will is not enough by itself. A person who thinks highly of himself does not get the crown.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (literally: the teaching says)

steps.whatToRemember: The crown of הקדוש ברוך הוא is for צדיקים who do His will and long for His glory. But it is only for those who see themselves as small.

phrases.english: therefore the verse says: 'to the remainder of His people',
to one who regards himself as leftovers.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר לִשְׁאָר עַמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the broad reading of step 6 by limiting the reward.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limitation from an extra phrase in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone who does God's will gets the crown.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only those who regard themselves as humble leftovers get the crown.

steps.title: Judging your own יצר and judging truthfully
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק (ישעיה 28:6). 'A spirit of justice' refers to someone who puts his own יצר הרע on trial. 'One who sits in judgment' refers to a judge who rules with complete truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for a spirit of justice': this is one who judges his own יצר. 'To the one who sits in judgment': this is one who judges a completely true judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: Since it already quoted ישעיה, the גמרא continues to the next פסוק. It starts explaining each phrase as a different kind of praiseworthy person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first phrase is read as inner justice: a person holds himself accountable and pushes himself to do תשובה. The second phrase is about a real judge. It is not enough for his ruling to be technically correct. It must be truly true, fitting the real situation.

keyTerms.meaning: One who puts his יצר on trial
A judgment that is completely true, fitting the real situation

phrases.english: 'And for a spirit of justice' —
this is one who brings his evil inclination to trial.
'And to the one who sits in judgment' —
this is one who judges a completely true judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט זֶה הַדָּן אֶת יִצְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next פסוק in ישעיה after the one quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Spirit of justice' means judging your own יצר. 'Sitting in judgment' means judging with complete truth.

steps.title: Overcoming the יצר and battling in Torah
steps.stepSummary: 'Strength' refers to someone who overcomes his יצר הרע. 'Those who turn back the battle' refers to people who argue back and forth in the battle of Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for strength': this is one who overcomes his יצר. 'Those who turn back the battle': those who give and take in the battle of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining the same פסוק phrase by phrase. Here it explains the words about strength and battle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real strength is inner strength: winning against your own יצר. The 'battle' is read as the back-and-forth of Torah discussion, where learners challenge and answer each other until the truth comes out.

keyTerms.meaning: Give and take (debate back and forth)

phrases.english: 'And for strength' —
this is one who overcomes his evil inclination.
'Those who turn back the battle' —
those who give and take
in the battle of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִגְבוּרָה זֶה הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the phrase-by-phrase reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Strength' means overcoming the יצר. 'Turning back the battle' means debating in Torah learning.

steps.title: The gate: scholars who come early and stay late
steps.stepSummary: 'To the gate' refers to תלמידי חכמים who come early and stay late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To the gate': these are תלמידי חכמים who come early and stay late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last word of the פסוק, 'gate'. This finishes its reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'gate' is read as the doors of the places of prayer and learning. The praise goes to those who are there first in the morning and last at night. Together with the earlier phrases, the פסוק becomes a list of the qualities that earn God's crown.
steps.whatToRemember: ישעיה 28:6 is read as a list of qualities: judging your own יצר, judging with complete truth, overcoming the יצר, battling in Torah learning, and coming early and staying late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

phrases.english: 'To the gate' —
these are Torah scholars
who arrive early and stay late
in synagogues and study halls.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁעְרָה אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the phrase-by-phrase reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'The gate' refers to תלמידי חכמים who come early and stay late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

steps.title: מדת הדין asks why ישראל is different
steps.stepSummary: מדת הדין asks הקדוש ברוך הוא what makes ישראל different from the other nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: מדת הדין said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם, what makes these different from those?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a short story in which מדת הדין, God's strict side of judgment, challenges Him. It asks why ישראל are treated better than the nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is phrased like a question, but it works as a challenge. The point is that it seems unfair for ישראל to get special treatment, such as miracles and the crown described in the previous פסוקים, while the nations do not.

keyTerms.meaning: The Attribute of strict Justice, pictured here as speaking before God

steps.confusionAlert: מדת הדין is not a separate power working against God. It is a way of picturing God's own quality of strict justice as if it were speaking.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה מִדַּת הַדִּין לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The Attribute of Justice said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
what makes these different from those?
phrases.notes: 'These' means ישראל. 'Those' means the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה מִדַּת הַדִּין לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ישעיה 28:5-6, which praises the righteous, to a challenge about whether ישראל truly deserve that special status.
steps.kashyaTarget: The special treatment that ישראל receive compared with the nations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Strict justice demands equal treatment. Why should one group be favored?

steps.title: God answers that ישראל learns Torah
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that ישראל are involved in Torah and the nations are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to it: ישראל occupied themselves with Torah. אומות העולם did not occupy themselves with Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: God answers מדת הדין's challenge. ישראל are different because they learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not favoritism. It is earned through involvement in Torah. This connects back to Step 9, where 'those who turn back the battle' were explained as people fighting the battle of Torah learning.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to it:
Israel occupied themselves with Torah,
the nations of the world did not occupy themselves with Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a real difference that justifies the different treatment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ישראל are favored for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: ישראל are different because they occupy themselves with Torah.

steps.title: מדת הדין replies that ישראל also sinned
steps.stepSummary: מדת הדין answers back with ישעיה 28:7: even ישראל's leaders stumbled through wine and strong drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: It said to Him: 'These too reel through wine and stagger through strong drink; they stumble in judgment.'
steps.whatsHappening: מדת הדין pushes back. It quotes the very next פסוק in ישעיה, which says that ישראל's leaders also sinned through drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God's answer was that ישראל learn Torah. מדת הדין replies that ישראל still have sins, so strict justice should punish them as well. The words 'פקו פליליה' are explained in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: The speaker in 'אמר ליה' is מדת הדין speaking to God, not God speaking.

phrases.english: It said to Him:
phrases.notes: מדת הדין speaking to הקדוש ברוך הוא

phrases.english: 'These too reel through wine'
and stagger through strong drink;
they stumble in judgment' (ישעיה 28:7).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּם אֵלֶּה בַּיַּיִן שָׁגוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges God's answer in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that Torah involvement makes ישראל worthy of special treatment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישראל also sinned, as the next פסוק shows, so strict justice should treat them like everyone else.

steps.title: Explaining the words פקו and פליליה
steps.stepSummary: 'פקו' means גיהנם and 'פליליה' means judges, each proven from another פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'פקו' means only גיהנם, as it says, 'This shall not be a stumbling [פוקה] for you.' 'פליליה' means only judges, as it says, 'And he shall pay as the judges [פלילים] decide.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two hard words at the end of the פסוק that מדת הדין quoted. Each word is proven by how the same word is used in another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the פסוק says that ישראל's sins make them deserve גיהנם and judgment. That is the full force of מדת הדין's claim: ישראל are also liable to punishment. The text gives no further reply, so the challenge is left standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Stumbled; explained here as referring to גיהנם
Judgment; explained here as referring to judges

phrases.english: 'פקו' refers only to Gehenna,
as it is stated: 'This shall not be a stumbling [פוקה] for you' (שמואל א 25:31),
and 'פליליה' refers only to judges,
as it is stated: 'And he shall pay as the judges [פלילים] decide' (שמות 21:22).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פָּקוּ אֶלָּא גֵּיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the פסוק quoted in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'פקו פליליה' means that the sinners are liable to גיהנם and to the judges' punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: God answers that ישראל are special because of Torah. מדת הדין answers back that ישראל also sin and deserve punishment.

steps.title: The שכינה leaves אסתר at the room of idols
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'she stood in the inner court', רבי לוי says the שכינה left אסתר when she reached the room of idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she stood in the inner court of the king's house.' רבי לוי said: Once she reached the room of idols, the שכינה left her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to explaining the מגילה. רבי לוי describes what happened to אסתר as she walked toward אחשורוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner court held a room of idols. The שכינה does not rest in a place of idolatry, so it left אסתר at that moment. This sets up her cry in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner court of the king's house

phrases.english: 'And she stood in the inner court of the king's house' (אסתר 5:1).
Rabbi Levi said:
Once she reached the room of idols,
the Divine Presence left her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתַּעֲמֹד בַּחֲצַר בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ הַפְּנִימִית. אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the side discussion on ישעיה and returns to explaining the פסוקים of the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When אסתר entered the area of idols, the שכינה left her.

steps.title: אסתר asks if she is judged for a forced act
steps.stepSummary: אסתר cries 'My God, why have You forsaken me?' and asks whether ה' judges an accidental or forced act as if it were deliberate.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: 'My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?' Perhaps You judge an accidental act like a deliberate one, and a forced act like a willing one?
steps.whatsHappening: אסתר feels the שכינה leave and cries out using the words of תהלים 22. She offers a first guess for why it happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was forced to enter that place, since she went to save ישראל and had no choice. She asks whether ה' is holding her responsible as though she had entered willingly. The question implies that this would not be fair.

keyTerms.meaning: My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? (תהלים 22:2)
An act done under force, beyond one's control

phrases.english: She said: 'My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?' (תהלים 22:2)

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא אַתָּה דָּן עַל שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד
phrases.english: Perhaps You judge an accidental act as a deliberate one
and a forced act as a willing one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה: אֵלִי אֵלִי לָמָה עֲזַבְתָּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives אסתר's reaction to the שכינה leaving in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the שכינה leave her? Is it because she entered the room of idols, even though she was forced to?

steps.title: אסתר wonders if it was because she called him a dog
steps.stepSummary: אסתר's second guess: perhaps the שכינה left because she called the enemy a 'dog' in her prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is because I called him 'dog', as it says: 'Save my soul from the sword, my only one from the hand of the dog.'
steps.whatsHappening: אסתר suggests a second possible reason. Perhaps it was the harsh words she used in her prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same chapter of תהלים, which is read here as אסתר's prayer, she called the enemy a 'dog'. She worries that this way of speaking was the real cause of losing the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: My only one, meaning my soul

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is because I called him 'dog',
phrases.notes: 'Him' here is המן.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Save my soul from the sword,'
'my only one from the hand of the dog' (תהלים 22:21).

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ שֶׁמָּא עַל שֶׁקְּרָאתִיו כֶּלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second possible reason, in addition to the one in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did she lose the שכינה because she spoke of the enemy with a degrading name?

steps.title: אסתר takes it back and calls him a lion
steps.stepSummary: אסתר immediately retracts and calls the enemy a 'lion', as the next פסוק in תהלים shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: She went back and called him 'lion', as it says: 'Save me from the lion's mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: אסתר acts on her second guess right away. She changes her words and calls the enemy a 'lion' instead of a 'dog'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the very next פסוק in תהלים 22, which switches from 'dog' to 'lion'. The גמרא reads this switch as אסתר correcting herself. It shows she took seriously the possibility that her words caused the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: She went back on it, retracted

phrases.english: She went back and called him 'lion',
as it is stated: 'Save me from the lion's mouth' (תהלים 22:22).

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזְרָה וּקְרָאַתּוּ אַרְיֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second possibility from Step 17 by showing how אסתר corrected herself.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אסתר corrected her words right away, calling the enemy a 'lion' instead of a 'dog'.
steps.whatToRemember: When the שכינה left אסתר, she searched herself for the cause. She suggested two reasons and immediately fixed the one she could fix: her words.

steps.title: Three מלאכים helped אסתר when the king saw her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the פסוק 'when the king saw אסתר the queen': three מלאכי השרת came to help her at that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And it was when the king saw אסתר the queen.' רבי יוחנן said: Three מלאכי השרת came to her at that moment. One lifted up her neck. One drew a thread of grace over her. One stretched out the king's scepter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק in the מגילה. רבי יוחנן explains that אסתר got hidden help from three מלאכים right when the king noticed her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the steps before this, the שכינה had left אסתר, and she prayed. Now the help comes. The first מלאך lifted her neck so she could stand tall and not be ashamed. The second made her look charming. The third stretched the scepter so it could reach her.

keyTerms.meaning: A thread of grace, meaning charm and beauty

phrases.english: "And it was when the king saw
Esther the queen"
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Three ministering angels
came to her at that moment:
one who lifted up her neck,
phrases.notes: So she could stand tall and not feel ashamed.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד שֶׁמָּשַׁךְ חוּט שֶׁל חֶסֶד עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: and one who drew a thread of grace over her,
and one who stretched out the scepter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אסתר's prayer and her taking back the word 'dog', the story moves on to the help she received from heaven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three מלאכים helped אסתר: one raised her neck, one gave her grace, and one stretched the scepter.

steps.title: How far was the scepter stretched?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long the scepter became after the מלאך stretched it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much was it stretched?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next few steps. The גמרא wants to know how far the scepter grew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the third מלאך stretched the scepter but did not say by how much. This one-word question opens a list of different opinions about the length.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: How far was the scepter stretched?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail missing from רבי יוחנן's statement about the third מלאך.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length the scepter reached after it was stretched.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: from two אמות to twelve, or more
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the scepter was 2 אמות long and became 12. Other versions say 16 or 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It was two אמות long, and the מלאך made it twelve. Some say sixteen, and some say twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the first answer: the scepter grew from 2 אמות to 12. The גמרא also brings two other versions of his answer, 16 and 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the scepter started at 2 אמות. They only disagree about how long it became. The phrase 'ואמרי לה' means there are different reports of what was said.

keyTerms.meaning: Cubits, a measure of about an arm's length
And he made it stand at, meaning he brought it to that length
And some say, introducing another version

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It was two cubits,
and he made it twelve;
and some say sixteen,
and some say twenty-four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: שְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'how much?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scepter went from 2 אמות to 12, with other versions saying 16 or 24.

steps.title: A ברייתא says sixty, like בת פרעה's arm and the teeth of the wicked
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the scepter reached 60 אמות. It compares this to the arm of בת פרעה and to the teeth of the wicked, which ריש לקיש reads as 'enlarged'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: It was made sixty. You find the same with the arm of בת פרעה, and the same with the teeth of the wicked, as it says: 'You have broken the teeth of the wicked.' ריש לקיש said: Do not read it as 'You have broken', but as 'You have enlarged'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a bigger number: 60 אמות. It then shows that this same miracle of something growing longer happened in two other places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בת פרעה's arm stretched out a long way so she could reach the basket of משה. ריש לקיש changes the reading of 'שברת' (broken) to 'שרבבת' (enlarged). That teaches that the teeth of the wicked grew long, the same kind of miracle as the stretched scepter.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Do not read it as ... but as, a way of reading a word differently to learn a lesson
You have enlarged, or made longer

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the text of the פסוק is changed. It is a דרש: a second reading of the word that adds another lesson.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: sixty,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא בְּאַמָּתָהּ שֶׁל בַּת פַּרְעֹה,
phrases.english: and so you find with the arm of Pharaoh's daughter,
phrases.notes: Her arm stretched out to reach the basket of משה.

phrases.english: and so you find with the teeth of the wicked,
as it is written: "You have broken the teeth of the wicked",
and Reish Lakish said:
Do not read "You have broken" but "You have enlarged".

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: עַל שִׁשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, larger answer to the same question, and backs it up with similar cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scepter reached 60 אמות, the same measure found with בת פרעה's arm and the teeth of the wicked.

steps.title: A tradition says two hundred cubits
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עופרן quotes רבי אלעזר, who received it through a chain of teachers, that the scepter reached 200 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עופרן said in the name of רבי אלעזר, who heard it from his teacher, who heard it from his own teacher: two hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last and largest answer: the scepter was stretched to 200 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא stresses that this number came down through a chain of teachers. That shows it is an old tradition and not a guess. It ends the list of opinions about the scepter.

keyTerms.meaning: Who heard it from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר עוֹפְרָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rabba bar Oferan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar,
who heard it from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher:
Two hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר עוֹפְרָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more, even larger, answer to 'how much?'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scepter was stretched to 200 אמות.
steps.whatToRemember: All the opinions agree that a מלאך stretched the scepter as a miracle so it could reach אסתר. They only disagree on the length: 12, 16, 24, 60, or 200 אמות.

steps.title: Half the kingdom, but not the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the king's offer of 'up to half the kingdom' had a limit: it did not include building the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king said to אסתר the queen: 'What is your request? Up to half the kingdom, and it will be done.' Half the kingdom, but not all of it. And not something that would stand in the way of the kingdom. What is that? Building the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the words 'up to half the kingdom' closely. It learns that the king was setting a limit on what he would give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Half' means he would not give everything. The גמרא adds that he would also not agree to anything that threatens his rule. That one thing was rebuilding the בית המקדש. So the king was really saying: 'Anything except that.'

keyTerms.meaning: That would come between him and the kingdom, meaning a threat to his rule

phrases.english: "And the king said to her, to Esther the queen:
What is your request?
Up to half the kingdom, and it shall be done."
Half the kingdom, but not all of the kingdom,
and not something that stands in the way of the kingdom.
And what is that?
The building of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲצִי הַמַּלְכוּת וְלֹא כׇּל הַמַּלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק in the story: the king's offer to אסתר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king's offer was limited: half the kingdom, and never the rebuilding of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: Why did אסתר invite המן?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why אסתר invited המן, her enemy, to her party with the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Let the king and המן come to the feast.' The רבנן taught: What did אסתר see that made her invite המן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes אסתר's invitation and asks why she included המן. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems strange that אסתר would invite the very person trying to destroy her people. The ברייתא wants to find her plan. This question opens a list of explanations, and the first one comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught, introducing a ברייתא
What did she see, meaning what was her reason?

phrases.english: "Let the king and Haman come to the feast."
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: מָה רָאֲתָה אֶסְתֵּר שֶׁזִּימְּנָה אֶת הָמָן?
phrases.english: What did Esther see that she invited Haman?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה רָאֲתָה אֶסְתֵּר שֶׁזִּימְּנָה אֶת הָמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק: אסתר's invitation to the feast.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: אסתר's reason for inviting המן to her feast.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: she set a trap for him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that אסתר invited המן to trap him, based on a פסוק in תהלים about a table becoming a snare.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: She hid traps for him, as it says: 'Let their table before them become a trap.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the first answer to why אסתר invited המן. She planned to catch him at the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים says an enemy's own table can become a trap for him. אסתר used the feast, a place where המן felt honored and relaxed, as the place to bring him down.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says, introducing a פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
She hid traps for him,
as it is said: "Let their table before them become a trap."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: פַּחִים טָמְנָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the ברייתא's question about why אסתר invited המן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אסתר invited המן so she could trap him at the feast, as the פסוק says, 'Let their table become a trap.'

steps.title: She learned to feed her enemy from her father's home
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says אסתר was following a teaching from her family's Torah tradition: feed your enemy when he is hungry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: She learned it from her father's house, as it says: 'If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives a second answer to the question of why אסתר invited המן. He says she was following a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר saw the invitation as a trap. רבי יהושע instead roots it in a Torah value she learned at home. The פסוק goes on to say that by feeding your enemy, 'you heap coals on his head,' so the kindness itself becomes part of his downfall.

keyTerms.meaning: from her father's house (her family's Torah upbringing)
your enemy (literally, the one who hates you)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
She learned it from her father's house,
as it says: 'If your enemy is hungry,
phrases.notes: משלי כה:כא

phrases.english: give him bread to eat, etc.'
phrases.notes: The next פסוק continues: 'for you will heap coals on his head.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מִבֵּית אָבִיהָ לָמְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the ברייתא's question, alongside רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She was fulfilling the פסוק of feeding one's enemy, a value she learned at home.

steps.title: Keeping המן close so he would not plot a rebellion
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says אסתר kept המן near her so he could not secretly plan a revolt against the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: So that he would not take counsel and rebel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a strategic reason. If המן were busy at her party, he could not plot against אחשורוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger was that המן would sense the king turning against him and stage a revolt. By keeping him close, אסתר kept him under watch.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
So that he would not take counsel and rebel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִטּוֹל עֵצָה וְיִמְרוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To keep המן close so he could not plan a rebellion.

steps.title: Hiding that she was Jewish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says inviting המן kept people from realizing that אסתר was Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: So that they would not recognize that she was Jewish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה says the invitation was a cover. If she had avoided המן, people might have suspected she was a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being friendly to the Jews' enemy made her look like a non-Jew. This protected her secret until the right moment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּירוּ בָּהּ שֶׁהִיא יְהוּדִית.
phrases.english: So that they would not recognize that she was a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּירוּ בָּהּ שֶׁהִיא יְהוּדִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent answer.

steps.title: So the Jews would keep praying
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says אסתר wanted the Jews to stop relying on her and keep davening for רחמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: So that the Jews would not say, 'We have a sister in the king's palace,' and stop praying for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה gives a spiritual reason. Seeing her friendly with המן, the Jews would not count on her and would keep praying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real danger was that the Jews would feel safe because one of them was the queen, and so they would stop praying. Her invitation made them think she had abandoned them, which pushed them back to תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: and they would take their minds off

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
So that the Jewish people would not say:
'We have a sister in the king's house,'
and take their minds off prayers for mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So the Jews would not rely on her and would keep praying.

steps.title: Keeping המן always within reach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says she wanted המן available at all times so she could catch him at the right moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: So that he would be available to her at all times.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי says that having המן nearby gave אסתר chances to make him stumble in front of the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This differs from רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר was about stopping המן from acting. רבי יוסי is about giving אסתר an opportunity to act against him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא מָצוּי לָהּ בְּכׇל עֵת.
phrases.english: So that he would be on hand for her at all times.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא מָצוּי לָהּ בְּכׇל עֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To have המן within reach so she could trip him up before the king.

steps.title: Hoping ה׳ would notice and make a miracle
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says אסתר hoped ה׳ would see that everyone, even the queen, was supporting המן, and would save the Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: Perhaps המקום will take notice and perform a נס for us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא gives a faith-based reason. She made it look as if no one was on the Jews' side, so that ה׳ would step in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that when the Jews look completely abandoned, even by the Jewish queen, ה׳'s mercy is aroused. Her honoring of המן was meant to bring about a נס.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
Perhaps the Omnipresent will take notice
and perform a miracle for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר: אוּלַי יַרְגִּישׁ הַמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To arouse ה׳'s mercy by making the Jews seem abandoned.

steps.title: Willing to die together with המן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says אסתר acted warmly toward המן so the king would suspect them both and kill them both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: I will be friendly to him so that both he and I will be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says אסתר was ready to sacrifice herself. She hoped the king would suspect an affair and execute המן along with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the most self-sacrificing answer. Her goal was to get rid of המן so his decree would end, even at the cost of her own life.

keyTerms.meaning: I will show him a friendly face

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
I will show him a friendly face
phrases.notes: Said in אסתר's voice.

phrases.english: so that he and she will both be killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר: אַסְבִּיר לוֹ פָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To make the king suspect them so that both would be killed and the decree would end.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as אסתר actually betraying the king. The friendliness was only for show, to make the king jealous and suspicious.

steps.title: The king was fickle
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says אחשורוש kept changing his mind, so אסתר hoped repeated exposure to המן would turn him against המן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: He was a fickle king.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל explains that because the king was unstable, אסתר kept המן in front of him, hoping his mood would flip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king who changes his mind easily could turn against his favorite minister. Seeing המן again and again gave that change a chance to happen.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
He was a fickle king.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מֶלֶךְ הֲפַכְפְּכָן הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The king's fickleness meant he could be turned against המן.

steps.title: Still need המודעי: she made everyone jealous of המן
steps.stepSummary: רבי גמליאל admits his answer is not enough on its own and brings רבי אליעזר המודעי's view that אסתר made the king and the ministers jealous of המן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי גמליאל said: We still need the explanation of המודעי. As it is taught: רבי אליעזר המודעי says: She made the king jealous of him, and she made the ministers jealous of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The same Sage adds to his answer. Fickleness alone does not explain how the king would turn, so he quotes a ברייתא: אסתר stirred up jealousy against המן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fickle king still needs something to push him. Being singled out for an exclusive party made המן look like a rival, both to the king and to the other ministers, and that jealousy brought about his fall.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Gamliel said:
We still need HaModa'i,
phrases.notes: In other words, my own answer is incomplete without his.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer HaModa'i says:
She made the king jealous of him,
she made the ministers jealous of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי גַּמְלִיאֵל: עֲדַיִין צְרִיכִין אָנוּ לַמּוֹדָעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבן גמליאל's answer by adding the jealousy idea from המודעי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She made the king and the ministers jealous of המן, which led to his downfall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the only answer in the list where a Sage openly says his own reason needs another Sage's reason to work.

steps.title: Pride comes before a fall
steps.stepSummary: רבה says אסתר built up המן's pride, because pride comes right before destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: 'Pride goes before destruction.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the אמוראים give answers, starting with רבה. He brings a פסוק from משלי: to bring המן down, first puff him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being the only guest at the queen's party made המן arrogant. That arrogance set him up for his downfall.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
'Pride goes before destruction.'
phrases.notes: משלי טז:יח

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: לִפְנֵי שֶׁבֶר גָּאוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first אמורא's answer, after the list of תנאים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To make המן proud, since pride leads to a fall.

steps.title: A feast that leads to ruin
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא both cite a פסוק from ירמיהו about preparing feasts for the wicked that lead to their end.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: 'When they are heated, I will make their feasts,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא give one shared answer. The party itself, with its wine and excitement, was the tool for המן's downfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק continues: 'I will make them drunk, so they rejoice and sleep forever.' The feast was meant to bring המן to the point where he would fall.

keyTerms.meaning: in their heat, when they are excited

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both said:
'When they are heated, I will make their feasts, etc.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו נא:לט

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: בְּחוּמָּם אָשִׁית אֶת מִשְׁתֵּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another אמורא answer, again based on a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The feast was meant to lead המן to his ruin.

steps.title: אליהו: she had all the reasons in mind
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה asks אליהו הנביא which opinion is correct, and אליהו answers that all of them are true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה met אליהו and asked him: According to whom did אסתר see fit to act this way? He answered: According to all the תנאים and all the אמוראים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the list with a story. אליהו הנביא says אסתר had every one of these reasons in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of choosing one answer, אליהו confirms them all. Her single invitation served many goals at once: spiritual, strategic, and political.

keyTerms.meaning: he found him, he came upon him

steps.whatToRemember: There were 12 or more reasons given for why אסתר invited המן. According to אליהו, all of them are correct together. She was acting on every one of them at the same time.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh came upon Eliyahu,
He said to him:
According to whom did Esther see fit to act this way?
He said to him:
According to all the Tanna'im
and according to all the Amora'im.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ לְאֵלִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole list of answers by confirming all of them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אסתר's invitation of המן was motivated by every reason given by the תנאים and the אמוראים.

steps.title: How many sons did המן have?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where המן brags about ״רוֹב בָּנָיו״ and asks how many sons that really means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And המן told them about the glory of his wealth and the multitude of his sons." How many is "the multitude of his sons"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק in אסתר and asks a simple question: how many sons is ״רוֹב בָּנָיו״? This question sets up the answers in the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״רוֹב״ (a lot, a multitude) is vague. The גמרא wants an actual number. Each answer that follows uses a different method to get one.

phrases.english: "And Haman recounted to them
phrases.notes: אסתר ה:יא, said to his wife and friends.

phrases.english: the glory of his riches and the multitude of his sons"
And how many is "the multitude of his sons"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה רוֹב בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new aggadic unit on the next פסוק, after the discussion of אסתר's feast ended with אליהו's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual number of sons behind the phrase ״רוֹב בָּנָיו״.

steps.title: רב says thirty sons
steps.stepSummary: רב says המן had thirty sons: ten died, ten were hanged, and ten went begging.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: thirty. Ten died, ten were hanged, and ten went around begging at doors.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: thirty sons, split into three groups of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know about the ten sons hanged in the מגילה. רב adds two more groups: ten who died earlier and ten who survived but became poor beggars. So המן's large family ended in disaster in every direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Going around to doorways, meaning begging

phrases.english: Rav said: thirty.
Ten died,
phrases.notes: Before the story of the מגילה.

phrases.english: and ten were hanged,
phrases.notes: The ten sons hanged in אסתר ט.

phrases.english: and ten went begging at doors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב, שְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.

steps.title: רבנן say the beggars were seventy
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say the sons who went begging were seventy, based on reading ״שְׂבֵעִים״ as ״שִׁבְעִים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: the ones who went begging were seventy, as it says: "Those who were full hired themselves out for bread." Do not read it ״שְׂבֵעִים״ (full). Read it ״שִׁבְעִים״ (seventy).
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן disagree with רב about one group. They say the begging sons numbered seventy, not ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They use an ״אַל תִּקְרֵי״ reading of a פסוק from שמואל א׳ (חנה's song). ״שְׂבֵעִים״ means "those who were full", and with different vowels it reads ״שִׁבְעִים״, "seventy". So the פסוק hints that seventy once-rich people ended up working for bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who were full hired themselves out for bread
Do not read it as ... but rather as (a reading with changed vowels)

steps.confusionAlert: ״אַל תִּקְרֵי״ does not mean the פסוק's text is wrong. It is a דרש that adds a second, hidden meaning by reading the same letters with different vowels.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
those who went begging at doors
were seventy,
as it is written: "Those that were full have hired themselves out for bread"
phrases.notes: שמואל א ב:ה

phrases.english: Do not read "full" (seve'im),
but rather "seventy" (shivim).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: אוֹתָן שֶׁמְּחַזְּרִין עַל הַפְּתָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב about the number of begging sons.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The begging sons were seventy, based on the אל תקרי reading.

steps.title: רמי בר אבא says 208 sons
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא says all of המן's sons together were 208, hinted in the word ״וְרוֹב״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: all of them together were two hundred and eight, as it says "and the multitude (״וְרוֹב״) of his sons."
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion: רמי בר אבא gives a total of 208 sons and finds the number inside the word ״וְרוֹב״ itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses גימטריא, where each Hebrew letter has a number value. The word ״וְרוֹב״ is meant to add up to 208. The next step checks his math.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: And Rami bar Abba said:
all of them together were two hundred and eight,
as it is said: "and the multitude of his sons."
phrases.notes: The number is hidden in the word ״וְרוֹב״.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: כּוּלָּן מָאתַיִם וּשְׁמוֹנָה הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 39, using גימטריא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 208 sons in total, hinted by the גימטריא of ״וְרוֹב״.

steps.title: The math adds up to 214, not 208
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that ״וְרוֹב״ actually adds up to 214.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ״וְרוֹב״ in גימטריא equals two hundred and fourteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רמי בר אבא's number: the letters of ״וְרוֹב״ add up to 214, not 208.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spelled with two vavs, the word is ו (6) + ר (200) + ו (6) + ב (2) = 214. That is six more than רמי בר אבא's 208, so his source seems not to match his number.

keyTerms.meaning: In גימטריא, the number value of letters

phrases.english: "Ve-rov" in gematria
equals two hundred and fourteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְרוֹב״ בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא מָאתַן וְאַרְבֵּיסַר הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 42.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר אבא's claim that ״וְרוֹב״ equals 208.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting the letters ו-ר-ו-ב gives 214, so the hint does not match 208.

steps.title: The word is written without the second vav
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is spelled ״וְרֹב״, without the middle vav, which equals 208.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it is written ״וְרֹב״, without the extra vav.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends רמי בר אבא: in the מגילה scroll the word is spelled short, so the count is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גימטריא follows how the word is written (כְּתִיב), not how it sounds. Without the middle ו, the letters are ו (6) + ר (200) + ב (2) = 208. So רמי בר אבא's number works.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (the actual spelling in the text)
״וְרוֹב״ spelled short, without the middle ו

steps.whatToRemember: There are three counts of המן's sons: רב says 30, רבנן say 70 of them went begging, and רמי בר אבא says 208 based on the short spelling ״וְרֹב״ (6+200+2).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"Ve-rov" is written without the vav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: ״וְרֹב״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 43.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the word is spelled full, with two vavs, which equals 214.
steps.terutzMaskana: The written form has only one vav, so it equals 208 and רמי בר אבא is correct.

steps.title: The King of the world could not sleep
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק ״נָדְדָה שְׁנַת הַמֶּלֶךְ״, רבי תנחום says the "king" is הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "On that night the sleep of the king was disturbed." רבי תנחום said: the sleep of the King of the world was disturbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק, the famous night when the king could not sleep. רבי תנחום says the word ״הַמֶּלֶךְ״ hints at הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מגילת אסתר, ״הַמֶּלֶךְ״ with no name can be read as hinting at the King of the world. So the turning point of the story is really הקב״ה "waking up" to save the Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: The king's sleep fled; the king could not sleep
The King of the world, meaning הקב״ה

steps.whyThisMatters: This night is the turning point of the whole מגילה. רבי תנחום's reading shows that the story's "chance" events are really guided by הקב״ה.

phrases.english: "On that night
phrases.notes: אסתר ו:א

phrases.english: the sleep of the king was disturbed."
Rabbi Tanchum said:
the sleep of the King of the universe was disturbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם: נָדְדָה שְׁנַת מַלְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new aggadic unit on the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״הַמֶּלֶךְ״ in this פסוק hints at הקב״ה.

steps.title: Angels above and Jews below could not sleep
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say both the angels above and the Jews below could not sleep that night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say: the upper ones could not sleep, and the lower ones could not sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a second reading: the sleeplessness was not only the king's but everyone's, in heaven and on earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״עֶלְיוֹנִים״ means the angels and ״תַּחְתּוֹנִים״ means the Jewish people. Both were worried about the coming decree, so the whole world was restless that night.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower ones, the Jewish people

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
the sleep of the higher ones (the angels) was disturbed,
the sleep of the lower ones (the Jewish people) was disturbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: נָדְדוּ עֶלְיוֹנִים, נָדְדוּ תַּחְתּוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second interpretation of the same פסוק, next to רבי תנחום's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angels and the Jewish people were both sleepless that night.

steps.title: רבא: it was literally אחשורוש
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the פסוק means what it says: King אחשורוש could not sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the sleep of King אחשורוש, literally.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the plain-meaning reading: the king in the פסוק is simply אחשורוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי תנחום and the רבנן, רבא does not look for a hidden meaning in ״הַמֶּלֶךְ״. The word ״מַמָּשׁ״ (literally) signals that he takes the פסוק at face value, which leads into the story of אחשורוש reading the royal records.

keyTerms.meaning: The Persian king of the מגילה

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of ״נָדְדָה שְׁנַת הַמֶּלֶךְ״: הקב״ה (רבי תנחום), the angels and the Jews (רבנן), and אחשורוש himself (רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said:
the sleep of King Ahasuerus, literally.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שְׁנַת הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third interpretation, the plain meaning, in contrast to the two hidden-meaning readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק refers literally to אחשורוש's sleeplessness.

steps.title: The king suspects a plot against him
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבא's approach, the גמרא describes the first worried thought that kept אחשורוש awake. Why did אסתר invite המן? Maybe the two of them are plotting to kill the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: A thought came into his mind. He said: What is going on here, that אסתר invited המן? Maybe they are plotting against that man (meaning me) to kill him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבא's explanation by telling us what was going on inside אחשורוש's head that night. His first thought is a suspicion that אסתר and המן are plotting against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that the 'king' who could not sleep really was אחשורוש. Now the גמרא gives the reason he could not sleep: אסתר's strange invitation to המן made him worried. The phrase 'that man' is a polite way of saying 'me', because the king avoids saying out loud that someone wants to kill him.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought 'fell into' his mind; it occurred to him
They are taking counsel; they are plotting
'That man', a polite way of referring to oneself

steps.confusionAlert: ״הָהוּא גַּבְרָא״ (that man) does NOT mean some other person. The king is talking about himself, and he says it indirectly so he does not have to wish bad things on himself.

phrases.english: A thought fell into his mind,
he said: What is this before us
that Esther invited Haman?
Perhaps they are taking counsel (plotting)
against that man (i.e., me) to kill him.
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying 'me'

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַלָה לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא בְּדַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבא's reading that אחשורוש himself could not sleep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחשורוש could not sleep because he suspected that אסתר and המן were plotting to kill him.

steps.title: The king questions his own suspicion
steps.stepSummary: The king pushes back on his own first thought. If there really were a plot, surely someone who loves him would have warned him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said again: If so, is there no man who loves me who would have told me?
steps.whatsHappening: The king argues with himself. If there really were a plot, why has no loyal friend warned him about it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step works like a challenge inside the king's own thinking. His first thought assumed there was a plot. Now he notices a problem with that idea: loyal people should have reported it. This sets up his third thought in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said again; he went back and said

phrases.english: He then said again: If so,
is there no man who loves me
who would inform me?

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (an internal challenge within the king's reasoning)
steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the king's first suspicion from Step 48.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king doubts his suspicion, since a loyal friend would have warned him.

steps.title: The king realizes he may have failed to reward someone, so he calls for the records
steps.stepSummary: The king explains to himself why no one warned him. Maybe he never repaid someone who helped him, so people see no point in reporting plots. Right away he orders the book of chronicles to be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said again: Maybe there is someone who did me a favor and I did not repay him. That is why people hold back and do not tell me things. Immediately: 'And he said to bring the book of records, the chronicles.'
steps.whatsHappening: The king answers his own question and decides that people stay quiet because he does not reward loyalty. So he immediately calls for the record book to check whether someone deserves a reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step answers the problem raised in Step 49. Silence does not prove there is no plot. It may only mean that informers expect no reward. This chain of thoughts explains why the פסוק says, right after the king could not sleep, that he asked for the record book. That is how he ends up discovering what מרדכי did for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of records, the royal chronicles

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the king's sleepless night was a chain of three thoughts: (1) maybe אסתר and המן are plotting against me; (2) but then why did no one warn me? (3) maybe because I never reward people who help me. This chain is what led him to the record book.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the turning point of the story happened through the king's own reasoning. His worry led straight to the discovery of מרדכי's good deed.

phrases.english: He then said again: Perhaps there is a man
who did me a favor and I did not repay him,
because of that, people hold back
and do not reveal things to me,
Immediately: "And he said to bring
the book of records of the chronicles."
phrases.notes: אסתר ו:א

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תירוץ (resolves the king's internal question from Step 49)
steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: דִּלְמָא אִיכָּא אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the king's question from Step 49 and links his reasoning to the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king guessed that he had failed to repay someone who helped him, so he immediately asked for the chronicles.

steps.title: The records read themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the passive phrase ״וַיִּהְיוּ נִקְרָאִים״ as teaching that the records were read by themselves, miraculously.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they were read': this teaches that they were read by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the פסוק and learns a lesson from the unusual wording ״וַיִּהְיוּ נִקְרָאִים״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say that someone read the records. It says 'they were read', without naming any reader. The גמרא understands this to mean a miracle: the book read itself out loud before the king.

phrases.english: "And they were read" —
phrases.notes: אסתר ו:א

phrases.english: teaches that they were read by themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיִּהְיוּ נִקְרָאִים״ מְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next words of the same פסוק and explains its unusual passive wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The chronicles were miraculously read by themselves before the king.

steps.title: Why does the מגילה say ״כָתוּב״ and not ״כְּתָב״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a wording problem in the next פסוק. ״וַיִּמָּצֵא כָתוּב״ sounds like something freshly written, so the פסוק should have said ״כְּתָב״, an old writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it was found written': it should have said 'a writing'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the word choice of the פסוק. It expected ״כְּתָב״, because the record had been written long ago.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״כְּתָב״ (a writing) fits an old record that already existed. ״כָתוּב״ (written) can suggest something being written now. Since מרדכי's deed had been recorded years earlier, the word ״כָתוּב״ seems out of place. The גמרא is setting up a lesson that will explain this odd word.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is only about wording. The גמרא is not doubting that the record existed. It is asking why the פסוק chose the word ״כָתוּב״ instead of ״כְּתָב״.
